1 غَرِثَ , aor.
غَرَثَ , (S, A, O, K,) inf. n. غَرَثٌ, (S, O,) He hungered: (S, A, O, K:) or, as some say, in the slightest degree: and some say, vehemently. (TA.) ＝
-A2- And accord. to Aboo-'Amr Esh-Sheybánee, one says, غَرِثُوا بِإِبِلِ فُلَانٍ, meaning They took the camels of such a one wrongfully: and a man says to another, وَيْلَكَ غَرِثْتَ بِى وَتَرَكْتَ حَقَّكَ [app. meaning Woe to thee: thou hast wronged me, and hast left, or neglected, thy right]. (O.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
